subject: Renewal discussion — Priority Response SLA, latency guardrails & burst capacity uplift
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@fastscale.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@fastscale.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal timeline & priority support options

Hey Marcus —

We’re starting our internal planning for the Nov 30 renewal and want to explore a few things before we commit:

- Priority response SLA (4-hour response) for production incidents
- Hard latency SLOs for our customer-facing endpoints at p95 under 250ms
- A short-term burst capacity option for Black Friday week (estimated +60% qps)

Can Redwood provide a clear path for these upgrades and any delta pricing? Also curious about contract term flexibility (12 vs 24 months) if we take an elevated SLA.

Attaching our latest capacity forecast.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Ops, FastScale
[Attachment: FastScale_capacity_plan_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]
From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fastscale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline & priority support options

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. High level: we can support all three items. Quick summary of options so we can align before I put a formal term sheet together: 

1) Priority Response SLA:
   - Premium SLA: 4-hour initial response for Sev1/Prod incidents, elevated on-call routing, quarterly war-room drills.
   - Add-on price: delta $Xk/mo (I’ll include TCO ranges after we pick a term).

2) Latency SLOs:
   - We can commit to p95 < 250ms for your standard traffic profile with agreed constraints (no more than 20% payload variance, model family X, and seq len cap of 512).
   - If you need strict p99, that’s a different tier we should discuss.

3) Burst capacity:
   - Short-term reserved burst blocks (1–4 weeks) can be pre-provisioned; automated fallback to compatible quantized variants if base capacity is saturated.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft a term sheet with two options (12m with smaller uplift vs 24m with committed discount).
- Marissa will scope the onboarding/ops handoff and run a short playbook for the Black Friday window.
- If you want, we can show a quick demo of our latency monitoring hooks next Wed.

Looping in Marissa (customer success) and Neha (sales lead) to confirm operational details and approval paths.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fastscale.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline & priority support options

Hi Priya —

Quick notes from the ops/runbook side:

- For the 4-hour response SLA we’ll add a dedicated escalation path (pager + Slack channel) and a named on-call for your account.
- To validate the p95 latency guarantee we’ll run a 2-week baseline test with your production traffic shadowed (no impact) and capture 95/99 metrics. That will lock the acceptable payload/sequence constraints we call out in the SLA appendix.
- For Black Friday burst: we recommend reserving a burst block now (to lock capacity) and then toggle it on during the window. We can include an automatic rollback plan if thresholds are exceeded.

I’ve attached a draft playbook and checklist. If that looks good I can schedule the readiness drill for the week of Nov 9.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Thanks for the context. A couple of commercial notes:

- 12-month Premium SLA: standard uplift 18% on current committed spend.
- 24-month term: we can offer a 10% credit on the uplift in exchange for the longer commit and a 30-day notice for early termination.
- We can include one pro-bono readiness drill per year as part of the 24-month package.

Marcus — please include these two options in your term sheet. Priya — if procurement needs a redlineable addendum, we can route it through legal and support a 48-hour turnaround for straightforward edits.

-Neha
